title: Superposition and Measurement in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Quantum superposition describes a fundamental principle where a particle exists in multiple states simultaneously until it is measured. Before measurement, the system's state is represented as a linear combination of all possible measurable states.

The act of observation causes the wave function to collapse, forcing the particle into one definitive state. This transition highlights the probabilistic nature of quantum reality, suggesting that physical properties are not fixed prior to interaction.
Furthermore, entanglement links the fates of multiple particles, meaning measuring one instantaneously influences the observed state of the others, regardless of the distance separating them.
